explanation: The V82A mutation eliminates a substantial hydrophobic cavity (~51 Ų reduction) in the S1/S1′ subpocket that atazanavir exploits for favorable van der Waals contacts with its inhibitor scaffold. This loss of complementary packing volume forces atazanavir into a suboptimal binding pose, weakening critical hydrophobic interactions without compensatory hydrogen bonding (no charge change occurs). The reduced side-chain volume creates a hydrophobic mismatch that destabilizes the ligand-protease interface in this key substrate-binding region, accounting for the measurable resistance.
